_comment: SYNTHETIC DATA. Hand-written to mirror the shape of a Google Places API (New) searchText response. No real venue data, no real reviews, no scraping. Used so the pipeline runs end-to-end with no API key and so the eval harness has a stable input.

places.editorialSummary: Warm neighbourhood tavern serving petiscos and slow-cooked mains in a wood-lined room.

reviews.text: Came with seven friends and they put us on the big table at the back. We were there nearly three hours and nobody rushed us once.
The vegetarian options are not an afterthought here, the mushroom rice is better than most of the meat dishes.
Music is at a sensible level so you can actually have a conversation. Rare in this neighbourhood.
Booked for six, table was ready, they split the bill six ways without blinking.
Service warm and unhurried. Wine list is short but everything on it is good.

places.editorialSummary: Vegetable-led kitchen with a small counter and a bright dining room off the square.

reviews.text: Everything is vegetarian and half the menu is vegan, clearly marked. My carnivore boyfriend ate everything and asked to come back.
Quiet enough to talk properly, tables are well spaced.
They took our group of six on a Wednesday with no fuss. Only downside, the kitchen slows down when it fills up.
Staff explained every dish. Felt looked after rather than processed.
Good for groups but book ahead, it is small and fills fast.

places.editorialSummary: Rooftop bar with DJ sets most evenings and a short sharing menu.

reviews.text: Incredible view and the DJ was on form, we danced until close.
Had to shout at the person next to me all night. Impossible to have a conversation after nine.
Food is snacks really, a few sharing plates, not a proper dinner.
Music so loud we gave up and left. Went for dinner, got a nightclub.
Great atmosphere if you want a party. Not somewhere to catch up with people.

places.editorialSummary: Dry-aged beef and open-fire cooking in a converted townhouse.

reviews.text: Best steak I have had in Lisbon, the aged ribeye is worth the price.
Came with a vegetarian friend and the only thing she could order was a side of grilled vegetables. Embarrassing.
Room is calm and the acoustics are good, we could all hear each other.
Took our table of six upstairs, service was attentive throughout.
Fine if everyone eats meat. Otherwise look elsewhere, there is basically nothing.

places.editorialSummary: Fast, cheap lunch spot with a rotating daily menu.

reviews.text: Good value, in and out in half an hour.
Fine but nothing special, feels like a canteen.

places.formattedAddress: Tv. do Monte do Carmo 5, Lisboa
places.editorialSummary: Ten-seat chef's counter, one tasting menu nightly.

reviews.text: A jewel. Booked three months ahead and worth every minute of the wait.
Only ten seats, the chef cooks in front of you.

places.editorialSummary: Tasting-menu restaurant with a wine pairing programme.

reviews.text: Exceptional from start to finish. Expensive but a genuine occasion.
Six courses, three hours, faultless service.

places.formattedAddress: R. de Campo de Ourique 88, Lisboa
places.editorialSummary: Busy petisqueira with a long communal table.

reviews.text: The communal table is perfect for groups, we met the people next to us.
Plenty for vegetarians, the grilled vegetable petiscos are excellent.

places.editorialSummary: Wood-fired pizza in a former bakery.

reviews.text: Sad to see it go, the best pizza in the neighbourhood for years.

places.editorialSummary: Small tasca with daily specials chalked on the wall.

reviews.text: Food is genuinely lovely, proper home cooking.
Waited forty minutes for mains and they forgot one entirely. Second time this has happened.
Charming room but the service is chaotic when they are busy, which is always.
Quiet and easy to talk. There are two vegetarian mains which is fine.
Booked for five, arrived to find no reservation on the book. They squeezed us in eventually.

places.editorialSummary: Glass-roofed dining room with plants and a Mediterranean menu.

reviews.text: The winter garden room is beautiful and surprisingly quiet given how full it was.
Menu is split clearly between vegan, vegetarian and meat. Everyone in our group found something.
We were eight and they merged two tables without us asking twice.
Servers were patient with a group who took forever to order. Lovely evening.
Gets busy at eight but the noise never becomes a problem, the plants soak it up.

places.editorialSummary: Standing wine bar with a handful of stools and a short plate menu.

reviews.text: Wonderful wine list, the owner knows every bottle.
Mostly standing, there are maybe eight stools total. Not a sit-down dinner place.
Great for two, impossible for a group. We tried with five and gave up.
No bookings, first come first served.

places.editorialSummary: Seasonal menu, open kitchen, long shared tables down the middle of the room.

reviews.text: Shared tables mean you end up talking to strangers, which we loved.
Three vegetarian mains and one vegan, clearly labelled.
It does get loud around nine when the open kitchen is at full tilt, but you can still talk.
They handled our group of six well, one bill split without complaint.
Service is friendly if occasionally slow to notice you.

places.editorialSummary: Family-run adega, tiled dining room, cooking from the north of Portugal.

reviews.text: Felt like being fed by someone's grandmother. Warmest welcome we have had in Lisbon.
Large table at the back took our nine people comfortably.
Meat heavy but there were two proper vegetarian mains and they offered to adapt a third.
Room is tiled so it echoes a little when full, but never uncomfortable.
Service could not have been kinder, they remembered us from a previous visit.
